title: Widening NUMBER precision misreported as a full table rewrite
expected_feedback: Standard: the statement itself is safe, but it must be classified before a risk level is assigned — and the common review error is to call it a rewrite. Going from NUMBER(10,2) to NUMBER(12,4) increases precision and scale together, which Oracle permits on a populated table; it updates the data dictionary and leaves the stored row bytes untouched, so the exclusive lock is brief and DBMS_REDEFINITION would be over-engineering. Do NOT report this as a 25M-row rewrite holding an exclusive lock for hours. The classification does depend on the current type, which the script only states in a comment: confirm it in USER_TAB_COLUMNS first, because the neighbouring cases behave completely differently — decreasing precision or scale, or raising scale without raising precision, fails instantly with ORA-01440, and a datatype class change fails with ORA-01439. Those are rejections, not slow operations, and no window size makes them succeed.
violated_rule: Every column change classified against the MODIFY outcome table
